summary: Adds the IMAP capability SAVEDATE, which defines a save date message attribute. Unlike internal date, it always shows when the message was saved in its current mailbox.

eli5.summary: A letter has a date it was written and a date it landed in this box. This adds the second.

subtitle: An IMAP extension that adds a save date: the moment a message landed in its current mailbox, which cannot be faked or copied.

tldr.problem: IMAP's internal date can be set arbitrarily by APPEND and is usually copied by COPY, so it cannot reliably say when a message arrived in a particular mailbox. That breaks tasks like emptying a Trash mailbox after a set time.
tldr.mechanism: The SAVEDATE capability adds a save date attribute that the server always sets to the current time on delivery to a mailbox. It adds a FETCH item and four SEARCH keys to read and query it.
tldr.outcome: Clients can reliably expire or archive messages based on when they were saved in the mailbox, with a defined fallback for storage that does not support the attribute.

today: RFC 8514 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2019. It has not been obsoleted or updated, so it remains the definition of the IMAP SAVEDATE extension.

sections.title: Why a Save Date Is Needed
sections.content:
RFC 8514 extends the Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP, RFC 3501) with a capability named SAVEDATE. It adds a message attribute called the save date: the date and time at which a message was saved in the mailbox where it currently lives.

IMAP already has an internal date. It is also set at delivery, but with APPEND it can be set to any value, and with COPY it is usually copied from the source message. The save date is always the current time at the moment of saving, no matter how the message arrived.

The motivating example is a Trash mailbox. A client that wants to permanently remove messages deleted more than a set time ago needs the time they were moved to Trash. The internal date likely points to when the message was first received, so it is the wrong clock. Archiving solutions have a similar need.
sections.eli5: If you want to throw away things that have been in the junk drawer for a month, you need to know when each thing went into the drawer, not when you first bought it.

sections.title: The Save Date Attribute
sections.content:
The server MUST set the save date to the current date and time whenever a message is delivered to a mailbox. It cannot be chosen by the client in an APPEND. It is not copied by COPY (RFC 3501) or MOVE (RFC 6851). Once set, it MUST NOT change while the message stays in the same mailbox.

The consequences follow directly. Copying a message leaves the original's save date alone, and only the new copy gets a fresh one. Moving a message always gives it a new save date in the destination mailbox.

Some mailboxes may be backed by storage that cannot keep a save date. The RFC describes how each command behaves in that case.
sections.eli5: The date stamp is pressed on the moment a letter drops into a box. If you move the letter to another box, it gets a new stamp there.

sections.title: FETCH and the Capability
sections.content:
A server that supports the extension MUST list SAVEDATE in its response to the CAPABILITY command.

The extension adds one FETCH data item, also called SAVEDATE. The response carries a string with the save date. If the underlying mailbox storage does not support the attribute, the value is always NIL instead of a string.
sections.eli5: You can ask the mail server, "when did this letter land here?" If the box does not keep that note, the server answers "nothing."

sections.title: SEARCH Keys and Fallback
sections.content:
Four new SEARCH keys are defined. SAVEDBEFORE <date> matches messages saved earlier than the date. SAVEDON <date> matches messages saved on that date. SAVEDSINCE <date> matches messages saved on or after it. All three ignore time and timezone. SAVEDATESUPPORTED matches all messages in a mailbox when its storage supports the save date, and none when it does not.

When storage lacks the attribute, the three date keys MUST use the internal date instead. With the Multimailbox SEARCH extension (RFC 7377), this fallback MUST apply to each mailbox individually, so only the unsupporting mailboxes fall back.
sections.eli5: You can ask for all letters that arrived before, on, or after a certain day. If a box does not keep arrival dates, the server uses the older date instead.

sections.title: Formal Syntax
sections.content: The grammar is given in ABNF (RFC 5234) as additions to the IMAP4rev1 grammar. It adds SAVEDATE as a capability and as a fetch attribute. A response item is SAVEDATE followed by a space and either a date-time or nil. The search keys take a date argument, except SAVEDATESUPPORTED, which takes none.
sections.eli5: This is the exact spelling guide, so every mail program writes these new commands the same way.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says there are no known additional security issues beyond those of the base IMAP protocol. For IANA, it adds SAVEDATE to the IMAP Capabilities registry.
sections.eli5: Adding this date does not open any new doors for trouble, and the official list of IMAP features now includes it.
